newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Act NZ's Prebble asks East to stop Peters' probe.
newsitem.headline: Act NZ's Prebble asks East to stop Peters' probe.

text.p: Act New Zealand leader Richard Prebble on Friday asked the Attorney General to call a halt to Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters' use of unnamed private individuals to probe the finances of Maori broadcaster Aotearoa Television.
In a letter to Attorney-General Paul East, Prebble asked what the legal and constitutional status of the inquiry would be.

"Does the matter come within Mr Peters' ministerial warrant? Why have the official investigators of the Crown, namely the Police, Commercial Division of the Justice Department, Commerce Department and the Serious Fraud Office been by-passed?" Prebble asked.
On Monday cabinet agreed to provide $4 million to keep the television network on air until June. The company produces Maori language television programmes for an Auckland audience.

Peters initiated his inquiries after revelations of links between Aotearoa and two men at the centre of the "Winebox" tax inquiry into use of the Cook Islands as a tax haven by New Zealand corporates in the 1980s.
Prebble also asked East whether Peters had a conflict of interest because his fellow NZ First MP Tukuroirangi Morgan was a former director of Aotearoa.
"Mr Morgan is also a personal friend of Mr Peters. Should associates of Mr Peters be investigating a friend of Mr Peters?" Prebble said.

"I am not making this allegation and I am very reluctant to reach this conclusion but a more suspicious person might conclude that this private investigation is really a cover-up. It is important for ministers to not only be beyond reproach but to be seen to be."
Prebble asked for assurances East had agreed to the process and it had been cleared by the Crown Law Office.
"If, as I suspect, you had no knowledge of Mr Peters' engagement of private investigators, your constitutional position is clear. You should advise Mr Peters to desist," Prebble said.

New Zealand's Serious Fraud Office said on Thursday it had launched a preliminary inquiry into the Aotearoa Television Network and there are other investigations by Commerce Ministry officials and the opposition Labour Party.
